items.title: 61427_Happy Caldwell oral history interview
items.q: Pastor Gense (unintelligible) had George Wein get up and deliver a sort of eulogy.

ctx.x: Yes, that was his wife. She asked for me to deliver the eulogy because I knew (unintelligible). Well, so when I get there, you know, I'd sort of written out something, not too long, Pastor Gense (unintelligible) had George Wein get up and deliver a sort of eulogy. Then he -- then I think someone in the middle of this thing -- I had to get up. Now, George Wein has already said some of the things I was going to say. It put me in a foolish position.

And then after I'd finished, after about a quarter of an hour of it, he reads out a sort of a eulogy that a priest in Montreal who knew Ray Nance (unintelligible), read this out. And in between we have girls singing, reading poems they had written and guys singing, and then -- I mean this went on for over two hours, and I think that's ridiculous. If anybody is seriously grieving for him, I mean you don't want to have to sit in that church for two hours. His mother was there. I mean how would she feel?
